To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and validated a testing protocol based in uniaxial compressive micropillar testing to evaluate the elastic modulus and plastic response of cemented carbides and that we found that plastic deformation/damage in the micropilars is correlated with the observed strain bursts.

the elastic modulus of fine and medium graine WC-Co alloys can be estimated by the micropillar testing technique, and the plastic response of the micropillared samples is correlated to microstructure and plastic deformation/damage within constitutive phases.

the uniaxial compressive behavior of cemented carbides can be evaluated by testing micropillars, and that the elastic response and yielding behavior of the micropillar are strongly related to the microstructure of the bulk material.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a testing methodology that can be used to evaluate the micromechanical response of WC-Co micromachined structures, which is a key aspect for the development of micromachined components based on WC-Co.
the evaluation of the micromechanical response of WC-Co materials.
the evaluation of the elastic and plastic behavior of cemented carbides at micrometer scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elastic modulus of WC-Co alloys does not change with the grain size of the WC phase, but the plastic response is strongly affected by the grain size.

the elastic modulus of WC-Co alloys is not affected by microstructural features, whereas the plastic response is strongly affected by the presence of the cobalt phase and its microstructural features.
the micromechanical testing protocol proposed in this study can be used to study the micromechanic response of WC-Co micromechanical components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the micropillar compression tests can be used as an efficient tool to characterize the elastic and plastic behavior of cemented carbides at the micro scale, and that the microstructure plays an important role in the yielding of WC-Co alloys at the micrometer size scale.

we have developed a protocol that allows to evaluate the mechanical behavior of WC-Co alloys at the micrometer length scale, which can be used to study the influence of microstructure, grain size and composition of cemented carbides in the mechanical response at the micrometer size range.
, by combining micropillar compression and microstructural analysis, we can evaluate the mechanical behavior at the micrometer size and correlate it to the microstructure of WC-Co alloys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed testing methodology can be used as a tool to evaluate mechanical behavior at the micrometer length scale.
the micropillar compression testing protocol can be used to evaluate the elastic response of cemented carbides and to correlate the stress-strain response with microstructural features.

the proposed protocol is able to provide valuable information about mechanical response of WC-Co micromechanics, and that the microstructural features of the material are key to explain yielding and plastic deformation/damage mechanisms.
